topic: Teen numbers as one ten and some ones

problems.desc: Part (b): the child explains why the ones decide the comparison of 14 and 12. Full credit for saying that both numbers hold one ten, so the tens are equal and the only difference left is the ones -- 4 ones is more than 2 ones, so 14 is greater. Accept the same idea shown with ten-frames: both have one full frame, and the loose dots settle it. Accept 'they both have a ten so I just looked at the 4 and the 2'. Half credit for correctly saying 4 is more than 2 without mentioning that the tens match. No credit for an answer that only repeats the symbol.

Part (b): the child says what went wrong when 17 was called one ten and seventeen ones. Full credit for the idea that the ten has already been counted once, so counting all seventeen again as ones counts the same ten dots twice -- one ten and seven ones is seventeen altogether. Accept 'she forgot to take the ten out first', or an answer that shows a full ten-frame plus seven loose dots and says that is all of it. Half credit for saying the answer should be seven ones without saying why. No credit for restating the number.
